newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq oil-aid plan seen within 10 days - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil-aid plan seen within 10 days - diplomat.

text.p: A senior Iraqi health official told the U.N. Sanctions Committee Chairman on Iraq that Baghdad would have its humanitarian aid distribution plan ready within ten days, a Western diplomat on the committee said Friday.
Sanctions Chairman, Portuguese Ambassador Antonio Monteiro met with the Iraqi health official ahead of the now-concluded sanctions committee meeting.
In talks with Monteiro, the Iraqi official reiterated previous statements made by U.N. and other senior Iraqis on the timing for finalizing the aid plan.

When asked if the committee discussed when the aid plan would come up for U.N. review, the western diplomat said: "The chairman had talks with the Iraqi Undersecretary of Health and he said possibly seven to ten days time."
Before Iraq can resume oil sales under the second round of the "oil-for-food" accord, it must first submit an aid plan and a new pricing formula for crude contracts.
Iraq received U.N. Security Council approval for new oil sales starting June 8, but has yet to resume liftings because it lacks a finalized aid distribution plan.

The "oil-for-food" accord is a humanitarian exception to sanctions slapped on Iraq after the invasion of Kuwait in 1990. Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over a 180-day period, mainly to buy food and medicine for civilians.
The western diplomat said the brief sanctions meeting also discussed progress in speeding aid delivery from the first tranche of the oil accord.
